idiom_name: repository-owned mutable.Map[Id, Entity] (Slick/Doobie return fresh case classes)
implementation_notes: Scala's main database libraries (Slick, Doobie) are query builders that return freshly constructed case-class values per query, so there is no session identity map to inherit and the classic structure is hand-written: a mutable.Map keyed by identity inside a repository/unit-of-work object, scoped per request or per transaction. Because case classes compare structurally, the map is the only thing that makes two loads share an instance; on JVM stacks that already use Hibernate/JPA you can lean on the persistence context instead. Prefer the hand-rolled map only when identity matters within one unit of work.
pitfalls: mutable.Map is not thread-safe: confine it to one actor/thread or synchronise access explicitly.
Structural equality of case classes hides identity forks: two equal values are still two instances, so every load path must go through the map.
A map held on a long-lived service leaks rows and serves stale data - scope it to the request/transaction and discard it afterwards.
